positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: District of Columbia, United States · On-site

positions.title: Sharepoint Administrator
positions.description:
•    Responsible for all the IMCOM Europe - Rhienland Pfalz  subsite collections. This includes custom development in a SharePoint 2010 enviroment, migrating previous outdated site to a new server, and knowledge management duties as well.
•    Acting as a consultant in regards to the United States Army Garrison (USAG)- Rhienland Pfalz public affairs office (PAO) and their public website.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
•    Responsible for the creation of the command’s Combined Asset Tracking Tool (CATT) to monitor the status and location of hardware, software, and mobile assets for the 7th Civil Support 
Command’s (7CSC) G6 department. It utilizes SQL 2012 SP1 database that is queried from list 
libraries on a SharePoint 2008 portal as the back end and a web interface that uses .NET 3.5, 
HTML5, and JavaScript.
•    Modifies and maintains the Civil Support Command’s (7CSC) public website in accordance to the U.S.Army Europe (USAREUR) web regulations, Operations Security (OPSEC), and US Army Public Office (PAO) guidelines.
•    Acted as deputy site lead to assist in status reporting and fulfilling other contractual requirements.

positions.title: Web Application Developer
positions.description:
•    Modified and maintained the 7th Civil Support Command’s (7CSC) public website. Duties include modifying layout in accordance of events, database management of articles and forum entries, image manipulation. I utilized Microsoft Visual Studio 2010, Microsoft SQL Server 2008, and Adobe Photoshop Creative Suites 4.0 to fulfill these duties. Additionally, I worked with U.S. Army Europe (USAREUR) in the migration of the 7CSC live public website database to the USAREUR DB enclave, while maintaining data integrity with a local development site.
•    Assist the G2 departments with custom reports for their Access TCO database. This includes 
creation of new triggers and stored queries.
•    Involved in a multi-modular .NET application that currently tracks a soldiers performance 
ratings within Microsoft SQL Server 2010

positions.title: Business Systems Analyst III
positions.description:
•    Was accountable for the maintenance and upgrades of the Army Master Range Plan (AMRP) tracking program. It is the repository for the validated, prioritized, and funded range modernization 
projects.
•    Aided in the completion of the DoD Information Assurance Certification and Accreditation 
Process (DIACAP) for AMRP.
•    Maintained and updated the Logistics Expendable Supply System (LESS) to meet the LOG 
division’s specifications. This includes adding new features such as email notifications, data 
validation, update reports, adjusting funding on new fiscal years, and alert messages on price 
changes. LESS is a VB6 application that is used by Ft. Eustis directorates to request supplies from log warehouse and track their yearly supply funding.
•    Web Table of Distribution and Allowances (WebTDA) is a personnel tracking program written in 
ASP.NET in Visual Studio 2008 with a SQL server back-end. Was responsible for modifying its design to meet programming best practices and security regulations. This included removal of the threat of injected SQL statements, adopting a common naming conventions, and normalization of the database. This was a major conversion from an Access application to a .NET web application.
•    Designed and developed the New Employee In-Process application (NEI) that is used to 
streamline the multitude of documents new hires to ATSC would have to fill. This web application 
was developed using the 3.5 .NET framework and some AJAX components.
•    Performance Based Management System (PBMS) is an application written in FoxPro 6.0 and used by various directorates within the US Army; was maintained and upgraded by me. Was responsible for modifications to its structure (such as directorate changes) and troubleshoot customer’s concerns.

positions.title: Web Application Developer
positions.description:
•    Had been the lead with the data management, migration, and the development of the upgraded 
Distance Learning Electronic Management Information System (dL eMIS) program. It initially started as a resource management tool to track the fielding statuses of distant learning courses and it was developed in Microsoft Project and Share Team Services.
•    Developed its upgraded counter-part with J2EE, Java beans, and SQL server 2000.
•    Merged the original Electronic Management Information System (eMIS) program with Mr. Ward 
Masons T3 database utility that Mr. Mason and Mr. Jim Trip use to track their courses thought their development cycle and testing.
•    Redesigned and developed an issues tracking application for the Q&A division of the Transportation School at Ft. Eustis using Access 2000.

positions.title: Application Developer
positions.description:
•    Developed and maintained a Management Information System (MIS) for the Navy at Dam Neck base. This web application utilized SQL server as a repository and .Net (Framework 1.0) environment and JavaScript to develop the front end.
•    Had also been assigned to acquisitions and facility management and maintenance, where 
responsibilities included the processing of every supply order, maintenance contracting, and purchase orders for the entire facility.
•     Was responsible for maintaining and modifying a paradox database system which used Power 
Builder to develop a interface

positions.title: Junior Programmer
positions.description:
• Designed and developed multiple logistic programs for multiple DoD customers (27th Flight line at 
Langley, Special Boat Unit 20 SEAL team at NAS Oceana, Combat Camera at Norfolk NOB, etc.) which utilized Access and Visual Basic 6.0.
•    Programmed the flash ROMS for the Janus XX.20 series barcode scanners and their label 
printers.
